messages:
maria-cs: Heads-up — NimbusX go-live tomorrow. Renewal flagged medium risk (low calls last week + 502 spikes). I sketched a short customer-facing runbook focused on caching, batching, and streaming to stabilize latency and demonstrate immediate cost wins. PTAL and add any must-haves.

maria-cs: Runbook draft (condensed):
1) Quick triage (first 10m): check console > per-route latency and error rate, confirm model falls back to smaller variant on errors. Link: https://console.redwood.example/customer/nimbusx/routes
2) Immediate knobs to reduce tail latency: enable prefix caching for frequent prompts, lower batch window to 20ms for interactive routes, enable streaming for long responses.
3) Cost/quality tradeoff: set quantization-suggested profile q4_8 on non-chat routes, keep full precision for safety-critical prompts.
4) Enable telemetry capture: add feedback hook param: capture_user_rating=true, send to cs-feedback endpoint.
5) Post-go-live follow-up (24h): run throughput vs latency snapshot and export prompt set for evals.

maria-cs: Example SDK snippet we can give them for prefix caching + streaming:
```js
// node example: enable prefix cache + stream
client.generate({
  model: 'redwood/gpt-6b',
  prompt: PREFIX + userPrompt,
  cache: { enablePrefixCache: true, ttlSeconds: 3600 },
  stream: true,
  batchHintMs: 20
})
```

tom-se: Nice. Two notes: 1) make the TTL recommendation conditional on their privacy policy (some tenants need shorter TTLs). 2) If they use server-side batching, recommend jittered client retry to avoid thundering herd on reconnects.

maria-cs: Good call. I'll add TTL guidance and a one-line policy checkbox.

anya-pm: From product side — add an eval checklist: sample prompt set (10 worst-case prompts), expected latency p95 target, and acceptable hallucination rate threshold. We'll use that to gate auto-fallbacks.

kevin-eng: Ops checklist: if 502s reappear, check model pool saturation (dedicated GPU queue) and fallback routing policy; quick command to inspect pool: `rctl pool inspect --tenant nimbusx --since 1h`. Also recommend temporarily switching to smaller model variant with `--force-variant small-v1` to keep UX.

onboard-bot: Reminder: NimbusX has security requirement SR-7 -> no external logs for user PII. Add that to telemetry snippet.

maria-cs: Updated runbook note: telemetry hook should strip user identifiers and send only pseudo_ids; offer them client-side feedback snippet to capture rating without PII.

maria-cs: Draft customer message (to paste in their onboarding channel):
"We have a short checklist to reduce latency and cost during your go-live: enable prefix caching (TTL 5–60m depending on privacy), set batch window 15–30ms for interactive routes, and enable streaming for long outputs. If you see errors, flip to the fallback variant and ping us — we'll analyze pool saturation. We'll capture non-PII feedback for quick quality checks."

tom-se: Can we add a one-click guide in Console: "Enable recommended perf mode" that toggles cache+stream+jittered retries? If not now, at least link to the exact toggles.

maria-cs: For now I'll include direct links and a short checklist with screenshots. I'll also create a post-go-live feedback capture Google form (anonymized) and link it in the follow-up.

anya-pm: Action items: Maria — finalize runbook and customer message; Kevin — provide `rctl` fallback snippet and confirm pool-inspect command output; Tom — prepare a short note about TTL/legal check phrasing. I'll own the eval checklist. Target: finalize by EOD so CS can send pre-go-live note.

kevin-eng: I'll drop the rctl examples in this thread in 20m.

maria-cs: Thanks team. I'll push the runbook to the onboarding folder and ping #cs for a quick read before sending to NimbusX. :thumbsup:
